How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow
all speakers to address the City Council. Please note that interactions between the City
Council, City staff, and the public during meetings are subject to the City’s Rules of
Decorum.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the online public
comment form at Public Comment. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00
P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for
their consideration, but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after
4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, July 15, 2025

 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Council Member Herrera Avila

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of July 1, 2025.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 15, 2025  2
   Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – JUNE 2025

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2024-2025 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for June 2025.

  D. ADOPTION OF THE 2025 SEWER SYSTEM MANAGEMENT PLAN UPDATE
  [RESOLUTION NO. 25-30]

  This item seeks adoption of the City’s 2025 Sewer System Management Plan
  (SSMP) Update, as required by the State Water Resources Control Board. The
  SSMP is designed to ensure the effective management, operation, and
  maintenance of the City’s sanitary sewer system. There is no significant fiscal
  impact associated with the approval of the 2025 SSMP.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Sewer System
  Management Plan is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) pursuant to Title 14, Sections 15061 (b)(3) (common sense exemption),
  15301 (existing facilities) and 15308 (regulatory process).

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 25-30 approving
  the City’s 2025 Sewer System Management Plan (SSMP) Update. The updated
  SSMP reflects the City’s commitment to providing a reliable and efficient sewer
  service, protecting public health, and complying with the regulatory
  requirements set forth by the State Water Resources Control Board (SWRCB).

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 15, 2025  3
   E. ADOPTION OF A RESOLUTION APPROVING A LAND AND WATER
  CONSERVATION FUND PROGRAM GRANT APPLICATION [RESOLUTION
  NO. 25-31]

  The City of San Gabriel has the opportunity to apply for Land and Water
  Conservation Fund (LWCF) grant funds through the National Park Service,
  administered by California Department of Parks and Recreation. With this
  funding, the state will award approximately $35 million in competitive grants
  for acquisition or development projects for outdoor recreation opportunities in
  communities across California. If awarded, the City would use LWCF funding for
  the renovation of Smith Park Pool and the replacement of the playground at
  the northeast corner of Smith Park. While there is no fiscal impact at this time
  as staff is simply requesting approval of the Resolution to apply for the grant
  funding, should the grant be funded, there is a match requirement of 50% of
  the awarded amount. Should the grant be funded, the item will be brought
  back to City Council for acceptance and appropriations of the funds needed to
  meet the match requirement.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 25-31 approving
  the City’s application for grant funds through the Land and Water Conservation
  Fund Grant Program.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH GRIFFIN STRUCTURES FOR
  THE PREPARATION OF A POLICE FACILITY SPACE NEEDS ASSESSMENT
  STUDY FOR $127,000 PLUS A 10% CONTINGENCY [RESOLUTION NO. 25-
  29]

  The San Gabriel Police Department building is in need of critical improvements
  to provide employees with an adequate, efficient, and safe working
  environment. Public Works staff developed a Request for Proposal for the
  Police Facility Space Needs Assessment Study Project and following interviews,
  staff determined that Griffin Structures is the most qualified and cost-effective

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 15, 2025  4
   firm for this project. The total cost for Griffin Structures to complete the Space
  Needs Assessment Study is $127,000 with an additional 10% contingency of
  $12,700, bringing the total project budget to $139,700. Resolution No. 25-29
  would appropriate the necessary funds into the City’s Fiscal Year 2025-2026
  budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a Professional Services Agreement with Griffin Structures and approve a
  purchase order in the amount of $127,000, and a purchase order for a 10%
  contingency using Police Facility Development Impact Fees (Budget Account
  124-751-40-96-586). Additionally, staff recommends adoption of Resolution
  No. 25-29 to appropriate the necessary funds for completion of the project.

  B. GENERAL PLAN UPDATE REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL RESPONSES

  Pursuant to Government Code Section 65300, each city shall prepare and adopt
  a comprehensive, long-term general plan for the physical development of a city
  consisting of a statement of development policies including eight mandatory
  elements: land use, circulation, housing, conservation, open space, noise, safety,
  and environmental justice. The City of San Gabriel adopted its general plan in
  January 1990 and a comprehensive update in 2004. On July 2, 2024, the City
  Council directed staff to obtain cost estimates for both a comprehensive and
  focused update. There is no fiscal impact associated with this discussion item,
  which is informational only. Should the City Council decide to move forward
  with the General Plan Update, the overall cost would be spread over a two-to-
  three-year fiscal period and would be funded by the General Fund. A 5%
  General Plan fee is accessed with every construction permit specifically for
  General Plan purposes.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council appoint two City Council Members to
  interview the three consulting firms along with staff and provide directions to
  finalize the selection process of the consultant.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – July 15, 2025  5
   C. MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH ARTS BRIDGING THE GAP
  ON BEHALF OF SAN GABRIEL VALLEY SYMPHONY FOR USE OF THE SAN
  GABRIEL MISSION PLAYHOUSE

  The City has been approached by a newly-established professional orchestra
  based in the San Gabriel Valley for a proposed partnership with the San Gabriel
  Mission Playhouse. San Gabriel Valley (SGV) Symphony is working in
  conjunction with an established non-profit, Arts Bridging the Gap, for
  development of this partnership with the Playhouse. While there is no direct
  fiscal impact for the proposed use, there is a potential for loss of revenue should
  the concerts not bring in adequate revenue, as expected, to cover the costs of
  Playhouse use. There is a potential economic benefit to San Gabriel based on
  artists and audience members visiting San Gabriel’s local restaurants and hotels.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve the Memorandum of Understanding with Arts Bridging the Gap on
  behalf of San Gabriel Valley Symphony, thus approving the waiver of certain
  costs and post-performance payment; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Memorandum of Understanding
  and any other necessary documents pending review and approval by the
  City Attorney.

  Alternatives to Staff Recommendation:

  1. Discuss alternate terms to the phased partnership with Arts Bridging the
  Gap and San Gabriel Valley Symphony.

  2. Send the item back to staff to determine additional alternatives.

  3. Other options that the City Council determines after discussing the item.

 8.  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

 9.  COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

 10. CLOSED SESSION – None.
